conventions.convention: Ordinary importance sampling assumes a known normalizer 0 < Z_p < ∞, real measurable f, n ≥ 1, and proposal positivity μ-almost everywhere wherever f times the unnormalized target is nonzero. The weighted integrand is zero on q = 0.
Self-normalized weights are W = p̃/q on q > 0 and zero otherwise; target interpretation requires q > 0 π-almost everywhere. A zero observed weight sum returns a no-estimate status.
For convergence statements, the self-normalized estimator is assigned numerical value zero when its denominator vanishes; almost surely this fallback is eventually unnecessary.
AC is assumed for the ordinary importance-sampling CLT, including its normal-law notation; the finite-variance identity is choice-free. Zero variance is allowed and yields the Dirac limit N(0,0).

The self-normalized CLT assumes finite second moments of both W and Wf and AC. The plug-in variance and standard-error consistency claims use those moments without AC and allow zero asymptotic variance.
Weight ESS is (Σw_i)²/Σw_i² for n ≥ 1 nonnegative weights with at least one positive weight. It diagnoses observed imbalance and does not certify coverage, finite variance, accuracy, or convergence.

load_bearing.statement: Compute S_n = ΣW_i. If S_n = 0, return the status no estimate: zero observed target weight. If S_n > 0, return ΣW_if(X_i)/S_n.
For each supplied IID proposal draw X_i, set Y_i = f(X_i)p̃(X_i)/(Z_pq(X_i)) when q(X_i) > 0 and Y_i = 0 otherwise. Return n⁻¹ΣY_i.

For measurable target and proposal densities with 0 < Z_p < ∞, measurable real f with ∫|f|p̃ dμ < ∞, q > 0 μ-almost everywhere on {fp̃ ≠ 0}, and IID Q draws, the ordinary importance-sampling estimator satisfies E_Q[μ̂_IS] = ∫f dπ.

For IID Q draws, q > 0 π-almost everywhere, E_QW_1 = Z_p ∈ (0,∞), and E_Q[W_1|f(X_1)|] < ∞, the self-normalized estimate converges almost surely to θ = ∫f dπ, with numerical zero on a zero-denominator prefix and an eventually positive denominator almost surely.
Under the unbiasedness theorem's hypotheses, E_Q[Y_1²] < ∞ implies Var_Q(μ̂_IS) = Var_Q(Y_1)/n. With AC, √n(μ̂_IS − θ) converges in distribution to N(0,Var_Q(Y_1)), including zero variance.
For nonnegative importance weights w_1,…,w_n, with n ≥ 1 and at least one positive weight, ESS_w := (Σw_i)²/Σw_i².

The consumers preserve integrability, IID transformations, finite second moments, and AC for the CLT. The ordinary-IS proof handles zero variance separately because the cited scalar Monte Carlo CLT requires positive variance.

The recorded seam is realized by ex-bootstrap-and-informed-proposal-particle-filter on the companion examples page. Its F3–F4 and step 3.1 use strictly positive finite-space proposals and explicitly multiply the normalized unbiased estimate by Z_1 to obtain E_Q[p̃/q] = Z_1. The arithmetic and normalization agree with the supplier algorithm and unbiasedness theorem; no self-normalized or CLT conclusion is imported.
